PHW colour and fill scales

Source: R/ggplot.R
phw_scales.Rd

  • _d scales are discrete and use the qualitative palettes (main, extended, accessible, highlight, rag, strategy).

  • _c scales are continuous, _b scales are binned. Both use sequential or diverging palettes (blues, teals, greens, gradient, orange_navy).

  • scale_*_phw_div() centres the diverging palette on midpoint.

Usage

scale_colour_phw_d(
  palette = phw_default_palette(),
  reverse = FALSE,
  key = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  neutral = default_neutral,
  aesthetics = "colour",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_fill_phw_d(
  palette = phw_default_palette(),
  reverse = FALSE,
  key = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  neutral = default_neutral,
  aesthetics = "fill",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_color_phw_d(
  palette = phw_default_palette(),
  reverse = FALSE,
  key = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  neutral = default_neutral,
  aesthetics = "colour",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_colour_phw_c(
  palette = "blues",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "colour",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_fill_phw_c(
  palette = "blues",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "fill",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_color_phw_c(
  palette = "blues",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "colour",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_colour_phw_b(
  palette = "blues",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "colour",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_fill_phw_b(
  palette = "blues",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "fill",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_color_phw_b(
  palette = "blues",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "colour",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_fill_phw_div(
  midpoint = 0,
  palette = "orange_navy",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "fill",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_colour_phw_div(
  midpoint = 0,
  palette = "orange_navy",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "colour",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

scale_color_phw_div(
  midpoint = 0,
  palette = "orange_navy",
  reverse = FALSE,
  aesthetics = "colour",
  na.value = phw_colours[["grey_light"]],
  ...
)

Arguments

palette

Palette name (see phw_palettes), a vector of colours, or a function of n.

reverse

Reverse the palette?

key

Name of a colour key, so each group keeps its colour across charts and reports.

values

Named vector of colours to pin to particular groups.

neutral

Group names to draw in grey, see phw_colour_key().

aesthetics

Aesthetics this scale works with, e.g. c("colour", "fill") to colour both with one scale.

na.value

Colour for missing values.

...

Passed to the underlying ggplot2 scale constructor.

midpoint

Value at the centre of a diverging scale.

Value

A ggplot2 scale.

Details

Every scale takes a palette name, your own vector of colours, or (for _d scales) a function of n. Everything else goes to the ggplot2 scale, so name, labels, breaks, limits, guide, na.value and so on work as usual.

Do you need one? After use_phw_ggplot(), or inside a phw_*_document(), plots already use these palettes, so a scale adds nothing unless you give it something to change: another palette, a colour key, pinned values, or a legend name. In a plain script with no setup, add one to each plot. A scale added to a plot always replaces the default for that aesthetic, whether it is one of these or a ggplot2 scale such as ggplot2::scale_fill_manual().

More than four groups. "main" has four colours and carries on into "extended" (twelve), so a chart with six groups starts with the same four colours as a chart with four. The first seven have a published source; see phw_palettes for where the rest come from. Past the end of a palette you get colours from the other PHW palettes and a warning.

Colours that stick to groups. By default a _d scale colours groups in the order they appear. To keep the same colour for a group in every chart and every report, give a key, e.g. key = "age_group". New groups get the next free colour and old ones never move (see phw_colour_key()). You can also pin colours with values, a named vector such as c(Wales = "#285087"). Groups named "Other" or "Unknown" are drawn in grey. (Only these scales know the group names, so a plot left on the default colours gives "Other" an ordinary colour.)

Colour-blind readers. Use palette = "accessible" for one chart, or switch every chart, table and widget at once: see phw_default_palette(). Add scale_shape_phw() or scale_linetype_phw() so groups differ by more than colour.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill = drv)) + geom_bar() + scale_fill_phw_d() + theme_phw()


# The same colour for each group in every chart:
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_phw_d(key = "drive_example") +
  theme_phw()

phw_key_reset("drive_example")
